quote: Example 1. Consider two series systems. Let G1(x) = 1 − 1/(1+x) and G2(x) = e^{−x} for x > 0. Suppose that (p1, p1, p3) = (e^{−0.05}, e^{−0.08}, e^{−0.22}), (p1∗, p2∗, p3∗) = (e^{−0.01}, e^{−0.21}, e^{−0.03}), (β1, β2, β2) = (2, 5, 6) ≽w (4.5, 5, 5.8) = (δ1, δ2, δ3) and (α1, α2, α2) = (1.1, 4, 6.5) ≽w (3.5, 4, 6.3) = (γ1, γ2, γ3). As mentioned in Remark 4, we choose the Clayton copula with generator ψ(x) = (θx + 1)^{−1/θ} for θ ≥ 0, set θ1 = 2 and θ2 = 4. Clearly, the conditions of Theorem 3 are satisfied. To plot the whole of distributions functions curves the lifetime of Y1:3 and Y1:3∗ on [0, ∞), we take the transformation (x + 1)^{−1} : [0, ∞) → [0, 1]. Then Y1:3 ≤st Y1:3∗ is equivalent to (Y1:3 + 1)^{−1} ≥st (Y1:3∗ + 1)^{−1}. Figure 1 shows that the distribution of (Y1:3 + 1)^{−1} is always larger than the distribution of (Y1:3∗ + 1)^{−1}, and this confirms that Y1:3 ≤st Y1:3∗.

quote: Example 5. Suppose Xi ∼ MOTL − G(1, βi, G1(x)) (Xi∗ ∼ MOTL − G(1, δi, G2(x))), i = 1, 2. Let Z1 and Z2 be two exponential random variables with continuous distributions G1(x) = 1 − e^{−λ1x} and G2(x) = 1 − e^{−λ2x} (λ1 ≥ λ2), respectively. Taking h(p) = −log(p). Then, the distribution functions of Y2:2 and Y2:2∗ are given by FY2:2(x) = ∏_{i=1}^2 [1 − e^{−ui}(1 − (1 − e^{−2λ1x})^{βi})] and FY2:2∗(x) = ∏_{i=1}^2 [1 − e^{−ui}(1 − (1 − e^{−2λ2x})^{δi})] for all x ≥ 0. ... According to the part (i) of Theorem 8, we set β1 ≤ β2 and u1 ≤ u2. Then, we obtain ∂FY2:2/∂β1 − ∂FY2:2/∂β2 ≤ 0. From Lemma 6, we obtain that FY2:2(x) is decreasing and Schur-convex. Thus, we have FY2:2(x) ≥ FY2:2∗(x), which implies Y2:2 ≤st Y2:2∗.
